mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the unemployment rate signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings and consumer demand, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of rising unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of falling consumption (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of tightening above 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the industrial production index above 1% signals an acceleration in economic activity and higher corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of accelerating industrial production (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous 3-month increase in unemployment rate above 3.5% and a decline in payrolls below -100,000 signals a deteriorating labor market, reducing corporate earnings and consumer demand, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of both rising unemployment and falling payrolls (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures above 2% and a decline in housing starts above 10% signals a deepening demand contraction, which reduces corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of both falling consumption and falling housing starts (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the industrial production index above 1% during a monetary easing cycle (federal funds rate below 3%) signals an acceleration in economic activity with supportive monetary conditions, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of both accelerating industrial production and low federal funds rates (t-test p > 0.05).
